name: Nkemdirim & Soh Hazard Overcoat
description:
A knee-length overcoat built around a chemical-resistant outer layer — not full hazmat, but enough to handle the aerosolized particulates, industrial runoff mist, and low-grade toxin exposure that is daily life near the Shelf's eastern industrial zones. The outer shell is a laminated barrier fabric in pale grey that can be wiped clean. The collar and cuffs seal with adjustable closures. A particulate filter hood tucks into the collar and deploys quickly. It looks like a slightly utilitarian overcoat until you notice the seal points.

Nkemdirim & Soh is a Shelf-based operation — two engineers who lost family to industrial exposure and built a business out of the need they saw every day. Their overcoat is not cheap for Tier 1, but community health organizations buy them in bulk and resell at subsidy. The coat has no tech, but the materials science is serious. It won't protect against a chemical weapon, but it will protect against the slow-kill reality of breathing near the processing yards.
what_it_says: You live or work near the toxic zones and you take your survival seriously. This is practical armor against a slow death.
story_hooks: Nkemdirim & Soh recently discovered their proprietary barrier fabric is being counterfeited with inferior material — people who think they're protected aren't
A corponation is quietly trying to shut down the company through regulatory harassment, and the founders need help understanding why
A journalist wants to wear one of these into a restricted industrial zone to document conditions — and needs someone to get them close enough

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian knee-length overcoat with an almost clinical aesthetic — structured and purposeful without appearing overtly hazmat. The silhouette is slightly boxy but not unfashionable, sitting with quiet authority on the frame. The pale grey laminated shell reads as professional, almost medical, until you notice the sealed seams and collar architecture.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders and torso to allow layering and mobility; tapered slightly at the wrists with adjustable seal cuffs. The cut prioritizes function and breathing room over body-conforming tailoring. Knee-length proportions allow full leg movement for fieldwork.
physical_description.primary_material: Laminated barrier fabric (pale grey) — a multi-ply synthetic composite with chemical-resistant properties and water-repellent outer facing. The material is wipeable and designed to shed particulates rather than absorb them.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly matte outer surface with a subtle sheen from the laminate seal. The lamination gives it a faint plasticity without feeling cheap — more medical-grade than industrial. Inner lining is breathable mesh-weave to prevent sweat accumulation during extended wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale grey primary (neutral, professional, conceals industrial dust). Dark charcoal or black trim at collar, cuffs, and hem for contrast and to highlight seal points. Optional muted tonal stitching in taupe or grey.
physical_description.closures: Front placket with magnetic snap or friction-lock buttons (faster than traditional buttons for emergency deployment). Wrist cuffs feature adjustable velcro or micro-clasp seals. Collar has a hidden seal track for the particulate filter hood, secured with friction-fit connectors.
distinctive_features: Integrated particulate filter hood that tucks compactly into the collar and deploys in seconds
Sealed seam construction throughout — visible on close inspection as reinforced stitching
Reinforced panel on left chest for carrying small tools or filters
Hidden interior pockets with sealed zippers for keeping documents or medication dry
Hem vent slits sealed with overlapping flaps for ventilation without compromising the barrier
Subtle Nkemdirim & Soh embossed badge on the right cuff (minimalist — just initials and a small circle symbol)
Faint wear patterns expected: scuff marks from industrial contact, discoloration where filters have been deployed
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover. Expensive for subsistence workers (Tier 4-5), but subsidized bulk procurement makes it accessible to community health programs. Signals neither corpo wealth nor street poverty — marks the wearer as someone in hazard zones by necessity, not choice.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by industrial workers, environmental remediation crews, hazmat handlers, medical responders in contaminated zones, and Shelf residents who cannot afford full protective suits. Wearing this announces exposure to slow-kill environments and a commitment to staying alive in them. It's the uniform of the survival-minded working class.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but meticulously maintained. Expected to show scuff marks, faint chemical stains that don't wash out completely, small creases from deployment cycles, and occasional patch repairs on the outer shell. The seals are regularly inspected and cuffs may show wear from repeated adjustment.
